assumptions.text: The referenced 'Designing an AI Pull-Request Review Agent' study was not attached to the working tree and could not be fetched from the linked GitHub repository in this session. Until supplied, the user's detailed architecture summary is the provisional architectural source; human approval must reconcile any omitted or conflicting study guidance.
assumptions.source: Repository inspection and GitHub fetch attempt, 2026-09-14

assumptions.text: Exact numeric SLOs, budgets, retention limits, and maximum supported PR size are intentionally provisional until justified by product evidence. They must remain configurable/documented and are not invented in SPEC-1.

invariants.text: A review finding may be published to GitHub only when it is structured, traceable to repository and diff evidence, deduplicated, evaluated for confidence, and authorized by the applicable confidence-weighted human-in-the-loop policy.

When the reviewed head SHA, retrieval freshness, evidence, delivery state, authorization, or policy outcome is uncertain, the system must not publish a GitHub finding. It must hold, suppress, supersede, or fail the run with an auditable reason.

decisions.title: Selective specialist-review architecture
decisions.text: The system will use an event-driven LangGraph orchestrator that routes eligible pull-request review work to independent specialists for security, correctness/quality, tests, and documentation. Their structured findings will be aggregated before any outward review action. This replaces a single monolithic reviewer and supports selective, grounded, high-value feedback.

decisions.title: Three durable state shapes
decisions.text: Production design will keep three linked but distinct durable records: code memory (repository revision, chunk/location, index/embedding version, freshness, tenancy); review truth (finding lifecycle, evidence, policy disposition, human feedback, GitHub effects); and time-ordered events (event type, timestamp, correlation IDs, actor/component, version/provenance, redacted payload reference). This separation makes retrieval, publication decisions, and audit reconstruction independently reliable and versionable.

decisions.title: Specification source boundary
decisions.text: For SPEC-1, the only authoritative sources are the user's requirements in this conversation, the repository itself, and Genesis workflow rules. External architecture studies and previously supplied architecture documents must not be used to add, justify, or revise requirements. Existing architecture requirements remain only insofar as the user stated them in this conversation.

decisions.title: V1 publication and automation policy
decisions.text: High-impact or blocking findings require human approval before publication. Lower-risk findings may publish automatically only under configured confidence/severity policy. V1 must not make automatic code changes or merge pull requests.

decisions.title: V1 tenancy and GitHub scope
decisions.text: V1 is single-tenant and initially supports only the user's own GitHub repositories. The sole source-control surface is GitHub Pull Requests, responding to opened, reopened, and synchronized/updated events with permissions limited to reading the repository/pull request and publishing reviews. The design should remain extensible to organization and multi-tenant support without claiming it is in v1.

decisions.title: V1 platform and dashboard
decisions.text: Use environment/configuration-based secrets, secure webhook handling, production observability, and provider-neutral abstractions where practical. Do not lock the specification to a particular AI model/provider. The dashboard is repository-user-facing for developers and engineering teams, showing review status, findings, severity/confidence, history, failures, and relevant health/operations information.

decisions.title: Production-target lifecycle
decisions.text: SPEC-1 must not invent numeric SLOs, budgets, retention limits, or maximum PR-size limits. They remain configurable and provisional until justified by product evidence, but measurable values for each must be defined before production launch.

decisions.title: Local durable queue for V1 single-tenant review build
decisions.text: SQLite is adopted as the current local and test implementation behind the DurableJobQueue boundary for the single-tenant V1 build. The queue interface preserves durable job identity, atomic leasing, exponential backoff, retry exhaustion to dead-letter, cancellation, and correlation to deliveries and review runs. Redis/ARQ remains the intended production asynchronous queue implementation when deployment requires distributed horizontal workers; SQLite is not claimed to provide multi-node horizontal queueing.

decisions.title: Production Infrastructure and Adapter Migration Model for Wave 1
decisions.text: SQLite remains the verified deterministic reference/local/test implementation for the existing V1 persistence paths during the production migration. It remains mandatory for local regression and reference validation. Redis/ARQ and Tiger Cloud are approved as production-target implementations behind existing contracts. No production default cutover is permitted until contract parity, failure-injection, and real-infrastructure validation have passed through Genesis gates. The migration must explicitly preserve: HMAC validation before processing, delivery idempotency, immutable snapshot provenance, current-head-SHA safety, evidence grounding, finding deduplication, calibrated severity/confidence, HITL for high-impact findings, prompt-injection isolation, secret redaction, specialist coverage integrity, publication idempotency, fail-closed behavior, no autonomous merge, no autonomous code modification, and existing V1 regression coverage.

decisions.title: Deferred Production Embedding Model and Vector Index Selection for Tiger Memory
decisions.text: W1-05 establishes the Tiger durable-memory schema foundation only. No production embedding provider/model is selected in W1-05. No production vector index is created in W1-05. Production embedding dimension and vector-index strategy are deferred to Wave 2, where they must be selected from evidence/benchmarking and then reconciled into Genesis before TigerCodeMemoryStore implementation. The existing V1 deterministic 128-dimensional feature-hash implementation remains the SQLite/reference behavior. The existing Tiger vector(1536) choice must NOT remain as an undocumented production contract.

decisions.title: W1-06 Scope, Non-Goals, and Adapter Boundary Invariants
decisions.text: Scope bounded to pr_review_agent/adapters/tiger_stores.py, pr_review_agent/adapters/__init__.py, tests/test_tiger_data_adapters.py, and optional migration pr_review_agent/migrations/002_repository_revisions.sql. Non-goals: no runtime cutover, no SQLite removal, no retrieval rewrite, no embedding model/dimension selection, no vector index creation, no Redis changes, no checkpoint changes, no LangGraph changes, no GitHub publication changes, no W1-07/W1-08 work.

decisions.title: W1-06 Scope Expansion: tests/test_tiger_schema_and_connection.py
decisions.text: Expand W1-06 task tiger-production-data-adapters scope to include tests/test_tiger_schema_and_connection.py because the approved W1-06 migration 002 changes the expected applied migration set from {1} to {1,2}.

knowledge.title: Initial architecture source
knowledge.text: The product architecture must follow the user's supplied flow: GitHub webhook; HMAC validation and delivery-id idempotency; Redis/ARQ queue; LangGraph orchestration; parallel security, correctness, test, and documentation specialists; hybrid repository retrieval; structured findings; aggregation, deduplication, confidence and HITL gating; GitHub inline review output. It also requires durable code memory, review truth, event/audit history, evaluation, observability, security, reliability, cost controls, dashboard, feedback, and drift detection.
